# shopify_collection (Resource)

A collection: title, handle, description, sort order and which products it holds, by hand (`product_ids`) or by rules (`conditions`). **A poor fit for Terraform unless you bootstrap a store or keep a few collections in a repository:** collections back navigation, but their texts and products are edited in the admin all the time, and every admin edit to a managed attribute is reverted on the next apply. Attributes you leave unset are not managed; the rules of a smart collection suit Terraform best. Membership is managed for collections with at most one non-shareable conditions source, which every collection made in the admin, with the older API or by this provider has. That includes a source another app created; Shopify may reject changes to it. Collections with several sources, a sub-collection or shareable source, variant-level selections or a condition Shopify can't express as input are read without membership: setting `match_type`, `conditions` or `product_ids` for them fails. Exclusions, the product order of `MANUAL` collections, the image and metafields are not managed. `publication_ids` publishes it to sales channels; removing an ID unpublishes it there. Destroying a collection deletes it with its publications and translations; the products stay. Menu items pointing at it lose their target, so add `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` to collections that back navigation. A collection that already has the handle, such as `frontpage` which every store has, needs `adopt_existing = true`; destroy then leaves it in place. Import with the handle.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "shopify_publication" "online_store" {
  name = "Online Store"
}

# Smart collection: products match the conditions, written in the API's own input shape.
resource "shopify_collection" "pflegehilfsmittel" {
  handle     = "pflegehilfsmittel"
  title      = "Pflegehilfsmittel"
  sort_order = "BEST_SELLING"
  match_type = "ANY"
  conditions = jsonencode([
    { productTag = { relation = "TAGGED_WITH", values = ["pflegehilfsmittel"], matchType = "ANY" } },
    { variantPrice = { relation = "GREATER_THAN", value = { amount = "5", currencyCode = "EUR" } } },
  ])

  # Removing an ID unpublishes the collection from that channel. Unset leaves the publications to the admin.
  publication_ids = [data.shopify_publication.online_store.id]

  # Collections behind navigation menus shouldn't be destroyed by accident.
  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

# Manual collection: products picked by hand, referenced so their GIDs never sit in the configuration.
resource "shopify_collection" "empfehlungen" {
  handle      = "empfehlungen"
  title       = "Unsere Empfehlungen"
  product_ids = [shopify_product.bettschutz.id]
}

# Every store has frontpage; adopting it manages the title, and destroy leaves it in place.
resource "shopify_collection" "frontpage" {
  handle         = "frontpage"
  title          = "Startseite"
  adopt_existing = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `handle` (String) The collection's URL handle, unique per shop. Changing it renames the collection in place and creates no URL redirect. Lower case, no whitespace: Shopify lower-cases anything else.
- `title` (String) The collection title.

### Optional

- `adopt_existing` (Boolean) Take over an existing collection with the same natural key instead of failing. Destroy then only removes it from state. Defaults to `false`.
- `conditions` (String) The rules of a smart collection: a JSON list of [`CollectionSourceInclusionConditionInput`](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2026-10/input-objects/CollectionSourceInclusionConditionInput) objects in the API's camelCase, one key each, written with `jsonencode([...])`, for example `{ productTag = { relation = "TAGGED_WITH", values = ["sale"], matchType = "ANY" } }`. Shopify validates kinds and values. Order matters; amounts and values compare numerically, so `"5"` matches Shopify's `"5.0"`. Reference metafield definitions and metaobjects by their resource or data source IDs, which differ per store. Products match asynchronously, so a new rule can take a moment to fill the collection. `jsonencode([])` removes all conditions. Removing the last condition and the last product deletes the collection's source, since Shopify keeps no empty one. A source with exclusions, which Terraform doesn't manage, is kept with them instead and then includes no product. Without exclusions, that is refused when Shopify made the source itself (no app, such as `frontpage`'s or one migrated from an older API version), because it can't be recreated (leave the attribute unset or keep one entry). Unset means unmanaged. A source another app created is managed too, but Shopify may reject changes to it.
- `description_html` (String) The description as HTML. Shopify repairs malformed HTML; the configured text is kept while Shopify still holds what it returned at the last apply, so the repair is no diff, but a later admin edit is. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `match_type` (String) `ALL` or `ANY`: whether a product must match all `conditions` or any of them. Required when `conditions` is a non-empty list. Null for a collection without a source. Unset means unmanaged. Null when the collection's membership can't be managed (see the resource description). A source another app created is managed too, but Shopify may reject changes to it.
- `product_ids` (Set of String) Product GIDs included by hand, whatever the conditions say. Reference `shopify_product` IDs, so products are created first and their GIDs never sit in the configuration. A product deleted elsewhere drops out and shows as drift. `[]` removes them all. Removing the last condition and the last product deletes the collection's source, since Shopify keeps no empty one. A source with exclusions, which Terraform doesn't manage, is kept with them instead and then includes no product. Without exclusions, that is refused when Shopify made the source itself (no app, such as `frontpage`'s or one migrated from an older API version), because it can't be recreated (leave the attribute unset or keep one entry). Unset means unmanaged. Null when the collection's membership can't be managed (see the resource description). A source another app created is managed too, but Shopify may reject changes to it.
- `publication_ids` (Set of String) `Publication` GIDs of the sales channels this collection is published to, usually from `data.shopify_publication`. **Removing an ID unpublishes the collection from that channel: it disappears there for customers**, so check the plan before applying. A new collection is published nowhere until this is set. A channel that publishes automatically (`auto_publish`) and isn't listed here is unpublished again. Only sales channel publications are supported; the publication of a market catalog is rejected. Scheduled publishing is not supported. Unset means unmanaged: publications set in the admin are kept. `[]` unpublishes everywhere. Needs the `write_publications` scope.
- `seo_description` (String) Search engine description. Null while Shopify uses the collection description. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `seo_title` (String) Search engine title. Null while Shopify uses the collection title. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `sort_order` (String) How products are sorted: `ALPHA_ASC`, `ALPHA_DESC`, `BEST_SELLING`, `MOST_RELEVANT`, `CREATED`, `CREATED_DESC`, `MANUAL`, `PRICE_ASC` or `PRICE_DESC`. A new collection gets `MOST_RELEVANT` when this is unset. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `template_suffix` (String) Theme template suffix, such as `special` for `collection.special.json`. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Collection GID.
- `source_id` (String) The `CollectionConditionsSource` GID that holds `match_type`, `conditions` and `product_ids`; null while the collection has none. The first condition or product creates it, and removing the last one deletes it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <handle>
terraform import shopify_collection.pflegehilfsmittel pflegehilfsmittel
```
